Date: 2027-03-15T09:10:00-07:00
Subject: CAIQ: third-party dependency matrix & evidence intake (Orion Health)

Hi Ella —

Thanks again for the time today. Per our conversation, the quickest path for the CAIQ crosswalk is to collect a short dependency matrix that ties each CSA control family to: (1) the Redwood control owner, (2) any third-party that contributes to the control, and (3) the artifact you can accept (policy, config screenshot, audit log extract).

I've attached a small template (caiq-dependency-template.xlsx) and a short guidance doc that explains acceptable artifact types. Could you share the following by end of next week?

- Completed dependency matrix (we only need controls that are in-scope for your assessment)
- Any vendor attestations that map to their control responsibilities (e.g., cloud provider SOC, managed service attestations)
- Preferred method for secure exchange (SFTP, secure Drive link, or dedicated intake email)

For tracking, Priya will coordinate evidence owners on our side and Monica will handle the artifact ingestion. Soojin will be available if you need help mapping control IDs back to the CAIQ file.

Next steps: if you can confirm the secure exchange method and drop the initial matrix, we'll review and follow up with any gaps or clarifying asks.

Thanks —
Marcus
VP, Solutions
Redwood Inference

Attachments: caiq-dependency-template.xlsx (spreadsheet), control-evidence-guidance.pdf (PDF)
From: Ella Romero <ella.romero@orionhealth.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: security@orionhealth.com, procurement@orionhealth.com
Date: 2027-03-15T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: CAIQ: third-party dependency matrix & evidence intake (Orion Health)

Marcus —

Thanks, this looks reasonable. A couple quick clarifications:

1) For vendor attestations, we prefer redacted PDFs with a cover letter calling out the control mappings (a single PDF per vendor is easiest).
2) We cannot accept public Drive links for any PII-bearing artifacts; secure SFTP or a Box folder with our procurement team is preferred.
3) Our security team will likely ask for a small sample of runtime logs if a control maps to logging/monitoring (they typically request 3 days).

I looped in procurement to coordinate the secure intake folder. We'll aim to return the initial completed matrix within 5 business days. If that slips we'll let you know.

Thanks — quick assignment so we don't bottleneck on intake:

- Monica: lead on artifact ingestion and initial validation. You'll take incoming vendor PDFs and the dependency matrix and push to the secure intake folder.
- Soojin: own CAIQ mapping. After Monica uploads, run the matrix against our CAIQ crosswalk and flag any control gaps.
- Marcus: point of contact for any scope decisions or expedited requests from Orion.

I created an intake folder and a short checklist in Drive: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1A2b3C_example_evidence_folder (permission set to restricted). Please do not share outside the team.

Monica — when you get the vendor PDFs from Orion, please: 1) check redactions, 2) index them in the evidence tracker, and 3) capture a 1–2 line note if the artifact only partially satisfies the control. We'll publish the tracker to Orion once we complete the first pass.
